children: Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on HDFC Bank, with a target price of Rs 950, saying the leadership transition remains the key near-term catalyst for the stock. HDFC Bank was up 0.21% at Rs 718.05 as of 10:58 am on Wednesday. The brokerage said an internal appointment could ensure continuity, while a credible external candidate could provide scope for a strategic reset and support a sustained re-rating.

HDFC Bank’s board on September 12 submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India for the position of MD & CEO, in order of preference, for a three-year term. Media reports indicate the likely internal candidate is Kaizad Bharucha, deputy MD & CEO, while the second name is an external candidate.

“An internal appointment could provide initial relief by ensuring continuity and limiting disruption,” Nomura said in its September 14 note. It added that Bharucha’s familiarity with the bank and its businesses “would also allow for a smoother transition”.

However, “a credible external candidate could offer a longer runway and a cleaner slate,” the brokerage said. “This could be more significant for the stock over the medium term, as a new leader would have greater scope to reassess strategy, challenge existing practices and drive a strategic reset.”

Nomura said that with HDFC Bank having “materially underperformed”, a credible external appointment with a strong operating track record “could therefore emerge as a catalyst for a re-rating”, particularly if accompanied by a clear roadmap on growth, deposits, margins and returns.

The board has also recommended the reappointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as whole-time director, designated executive director, for one year and the appointment of Jimmy Tata as whole-time director for three years, subject to RBI approval. It has approved one additional whole-time director position, taking the total to four WTDs in addition to the MD & CEO. The additional position will be filled in consultation with the incoming CEO.

Separately, Bahrain’s High Civil Court has rejected all seven cases filed against HDFC Bank by investors in the Credit Suisse AT1 bonds matter. The final two proceedings were rejected on September 9, following five similar cases dismissed during July and August. The court also directed investors to bear the costs.

Nomura said the leadership transition remains the “more important near-term stock catalyst” and maintained its ‘Buy’ rating. It values HDFC Bank at 1.9x March 2028F BVPS to arrive at a target price of Rs 950, with subsidiaries contributing Rs 105 per share.

title: HDFC Bank in green; Nomura sees external CEO appointment as potential re-rating catalyst, retains ‘Buy’
